message.content:
Okay, here's the negation of the text within the brackets, keeping the rest of the sentence intact:

'Can you help me draft a power of attorney document tailored to my needs?'

---

Now, here's a multi-paragraph example, framed as a response to the implied question (whether someone *can* help draft a power of attorney). This demonstrates the positive assertion that replaces the negated portion:

Drafting a power of attorney document requires a solid understanding of legal terminology and the specific requirements of the jurisdiction where it will be used. Thankfully, I *can* help you draft a document tailored to your needs. My capabilities extend to structuring the document with appropriate clauses for financial, healthcare, and other crucial decision-making powers. I can also integrate specific instructions you have regarding the scope of the attorney's authority.

The process begins with gathering information about your assets, your wishes, and the person you intend to appoint as your attorney-in-fact. I will ask a series of questions to ensure I have a complete picture of your circumstances. Based on your responses, I can generate a first draft that covers the necessary legal ground. It's important to remember, however, that while I can draft the document, I am not a substitute for legal counsel. 

I can customize the document to include provisions for things like durable power of attorney (remaining valid even if you become incapacitated), springing power of attorney (becoming effective only upon a specific event), and limitations on the attorney-in-fact’s power. I also ensure the document clearly defines how and when the power of attorney can be revoked. This ensures that your intentions are accurately and legally documented. Finally, I will present you with the document in a clear, organized format that you can then review with your legal advisor.
